How much does it cost to run a fridge freezer?

Fridge freezers run all year, so even a modest one adds up. The yearly kWh figure is printed on the energy label.

Cost per year
£65.80
About £5.48 a month at 26.32p/kWh.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

A typical fridge freezer uses about 250 kWh a year (100–500 kWh depending on size and efficiency). At the current price cap rate that's about £65.80 a year, or £5.48 a month.

Worth knowing: CSE gives 300W, but that's only while the compressor runs. It switches on and off all day, so the yearly kWh on the energy label is more accurate.

Source for the typical figure: Energy label figure (estimate). See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Find the kWh/annum figure on the energy label and set the slider to match.
  • Keep the fridge at 3–5°C and the freezer at −18°C.
  • Leave space behind for air to circulate, and defrost the freezer if ice builds up.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a fridge freezer per month?

About £5.48 a month for a model using 250 kWh a year, at 26.32p/kWh.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my fridge freezer's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
